lines: On a phone beside the bike, a thumb has to land. At a desk, the keyboard has to show where it is.
Every control now takes a tap across forty-four pixels, even where it is drawn smaller. A switch still looks twenty-four pixels tall.
The first run found thirty-four controls a tap could miss, on five screens. Twenty-four were in Settings.
Mid-ride on a phone, the target is forty-eight pixels. The class ride's Pause and Leave now draw at forty-eight.
At a desk, Tab stops on every control in turn, and each one shows its ring. A class card draws it around its cover.
Take the focus style away, and the check fails on every screen. Fifteen screens are tapped and tabbed on every run.
Settings, from a phone to the full screen.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
